text:
This world’s a city full of straying streets,
And death’s the market-place where each one meets.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 5
plain: Everyone takes a different road, and every road ends in the same place.

text:
Let th’ event,
That never-erring arbitrator, tell us
When we know all ourselves; and let us follow
The becking of our chance.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Outcomes are the only honest judge. Do the work, then let results tell you who you are.

text:
Their knot of love,
Tied, weaved, entangled, with so true, so long,
And with a finger of so deep a cunning,
May be outworn, never undone.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: A bond built over years can wear thin, but it does not come apart.

location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: Two real friends are each other's whole world.

text:
Whilst Palamon is with me, let me perish
If I think this our prison!
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: With the right person beside you, the worst place stops feeling like a cage.

text:
I am sure, a more content; and all those pleasures
That woo the wills of men to vanity
I see through now, and am sufficient
To tell the world ’tis but a gaudy shadow
That old Time as he passes by takes with him.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: Most of what tempts people is a shiny shadow that time carries off anyway.

text:
Come what can come,
The worst is death; I will not leave the kingdom.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Once you accept the worst case, you stop running from what you want.

text:
Their valiant temper
Men lose when they incline to treachery;
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Cut one corner on your own honor and the nerve goes out of you.

text:
Fortune, whose title is as momentary,
As to us death is certain.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Luck never holds a title for long. Death always does.

text:
And with our patience anger tottering Fortune,
Who at her certain’st reels.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Stay calm and luck gets rattled. Even at her best she is unsteady.

text:
That we should things desire, which do cost us
The loss of our desire! That naught could buy
Dear love, but loss of dear love!
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Sometimes the price of the thing you want is the thing you wanted.

text:
What things you make of us! For what we lack
We laugh, for what we have are sorry, still
Are children in some kind. Let us be thankful
For that which is, and with you leave dispute
That are above our question.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: We want what we lack and grieve what we have. Be thankful for what is.

text:
Two lads that thought there was no more behind
But such a day tomorrow as today,
And to be boy eternal.
plain: Youth feels like every tomorrow will match today. It does not.

text: Temptations have since then been born to ’s!
plain: Innocence ends the day temptation shows up, and it always does.

text: Our praises are our wages.
plain: Praise is what people pay in. Don't work only for it.
The right company makes the long days short and clears the heavy thoughts.

text:
I may be negligent, foolish, and fearful;
In every one of these no man is free,
But that his negligence, his folly, fear,
Among the infinite doings of the world,
Sometime puts forth.
plain: Everybody is lazy, foolish and scared sometimes. Own it and keep going.

text:
I know not: but I am sure ’tis safer to
Avoid what’s grown than question how ’tis born.
plain: When trouble is already big, stop asking how it started and get out of the way.

text:
There’s some ill planet reigns:
I must be patient till the heavens look
With an aspect more favourable.
plain: Some seasons are just bad. Hold steady until the luck turns.

text:
Alack, for lesser knowledge! How accurs’d
In being so blest! There may be in the cup
A spider steep’d, and one may drink, depart,
And yet partake no venom, for his knowledge
Is not infected; but if one present
Th’ abhorr’d ingredient to his eye, make known
How he hath drunk, he cracks his gorge, his sides,
With violent hefts. I have drunk, and seen the spider.
plain: Suspicion poisons you. Once you have seen the spider in the cup, you cannot unsee it.

text:
The silence often of pure innocence
Persuades, when speaking fails.
plain: Sometimes quiet integrity wins what arguing can't.

text: I am a feather for each wind that blows.
plain: No center, no direction. Every mood pushes you around.

text:
It is an heretic that makes the fire,
Not she which burns in ’t.
plain: The shame belongs to the one who lights the fire, not the one standing in it.

text:
I doubt not, then, but innocence shall make
False accusation blush, and tyranny
Tremble at patience.
plain: Patience under false blame makes the accuser nervous.

text:
What’s gone and what’s past help,
Should be past grief.
plain: If you can't fix it, stop paying for it with your sleep.
